 Flood Illustration. Acting Head of the Data, Information, and Disaster Communication Center at BNPB, Berton SP Panjaitan, disclosed that there are five districts in Indonesia currently on high alert for flood disasters. (KOMPAS.com/ PUTU AYU PRATAMA SUGIYO) 
 Writer Firda Janati | Editor Bilal Ramadhan 
 JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com - Acting Head of the Data, Information, and Disaster Communication Center at BNPB, Berton SP Panjaitan, disclosed that there are five districts in Indonesia currently on high alert for flood disasters.
 The five districts under high alert status are Rangsang Barat District in Meranti Islands Regency, Riau; Lima Koto District in Mukomuko Regency, Bengkulu; Moga District in Pemalang Regency, Central Java; Margasari District in Tegal Regency, Central Java; and Songgom District in Brebes Regency, Central Java.
 "There are five districts in Indonesia on high alert for flood disasters from November 15 to 18, 2026," said Berton during a press conference held online and broadcast via BNPB's YouTube channel on Monday (November 16, 2026).
 In response to these predictions, the BPBD (Regional Disaster Management Agency) along with local governments has taken action to address the evolving conditions of wet hydrometeorological disasters in various regions.
 "During a coordination meeting to address wet hydrometeorological disasters in Aceh and North Sumatra starting today, the Head of BNPB instructed the readiness of weather modification operation fleets or OMC," Berton added.
 The weather modification operation will be stationed at bases at Sultan Iskandar Muda Airport in Banda Aceh and Soewondo Air Force Base in North Sumatra, each supported by two OMC fleets.
 "This is part of our efforts to anticipate extreme weather potential and minimize disaster impacts on the community," he stated.
 As for tomorrow's weather forecast, Tuesday (November 17, 2026), there is potential for moderate to heavy rain in Bali, Central Java, West Kalimantan, East Kalimantan, Bangka Belitung Islands, Riau, West Sulawesi, South Sulawesi, and West Sumatra.
 "We always urge communities in affected regions and maritime transport users to increase their vigilance concerning potential moderate to heavy rains and sea waves," said Berton.
 Overall, BNPB has reported that there are currently 22 disaster occurrences in Indonesia, predominantly caused by wet hydrometeorological disasters.
 "From 2,354 incidents on November 13, 2026, as previously reported to the Indonesian public, it has now increased to 2,376 incidents as of today, November 16, 2026," he explained.
 Berton elaborated that these 22 disasters include flooding on Sumatra Island, extreme weather on Java Island, and forest and land fires in central Indonesia, specifically on Sulawesi Island and eastern Java.
 "We hope this serves as a wake-up call to enhance our collective preparedness regarding potential disasters around us, especially those occurring in West Java and Central Java," he concluded.
